draft.title: Solving exponential equations
card: To solve an equation with x in the power, take logarithms of both sides. This brings the power down: 3ˣ = 20 becomes x log 3 = log 20.
Then divide: x = log 20 ÷ log 3 ≈ 2.73. Use the same base on both sides. A calculator's log or ln button both work.
When the base is e, use the natural log ln, because ln undoes eˣ. So eˣ = 5 gives x = ln 5 ≈ 1.61.
Get the power on its own first. For 2 × 3ˣ = 40, divide both sides by 2 to get 3ˣ = 20, then take logarithms.
draft.remember: Isolate the power, take logs of both sides, then divide. Use ln for base e.

a.q: Solve 5ˣ = 40. Give x to 2 decimal places.
a.why: Taking logs gives x log 5 = log 40, so x = log 40 ÷ log 5 ≈ 2.29. Dividing 40 by 5 to get 8 is tempting, but that treats 5ˣ as 5 × x, and it is not.
a.clue: Bring the power down with logs, then divide the two log values.

b.q: Solve 2eˣ = 14. Give x to 2 decimal places.
b.why: Divide both sides by 2 to get eˣ = 7, so x = ln 7 ≈ 1.95. Taking ln 14 straight away gives 2.64, which skips the step of getting eˣ alone, so it is wrong.
b.clue: Get eˣ on its own before you use ln.

check.summary: No problems found. Both answers check out: log 40 ÷ log 5 ≈ 2.29 and ln 7 ≈ 1.95. The distractors match common errors (40 ÷ 5, the inverted ratio, ln 40, ln 14).
